meta.title: Containerizing and Publishing an App with Amazon ECR

slides.title: Containerizing and Publishing an App with Amazon ECR
Two-Instance Workflow
slides.lead:
A small Flask app is containerized on one EC2 instance, pushed to Amazon ECR (Elastic Container Registry), then run unchanged on a second EC2 instance
Needed before starting: an AWS account, VS Code with the Remote-SSH extension, and basic Docker commands from the earlier container session
slides.notes: Practical overview (TR Slide 26). The same packaged image runs on both instances; only the configuration changes.

items.text: Launch an x86 build EC2 instance and connect over SSH
Install Docker on the build instance and verify it from VS Code
Write a small Flask app reading its message from an environment variable
Write a Dockerfile and build the image, observing layer caching on rebuild
Run the image locally on the build instance and test it with curl
Create an immutable-tag ECR repository, attach a push role, log in to ECR, and push the image tagged v1

items.text: Launch a second EC2 instance with an ECR-pull role, port 80 open, and Docker installed
Log in to ECR and pull the v1 image
Run the pulled image mapped to port 80 and verify it with curl
Open the public IP in a browser to confirm the deployed page
Clean up: remove the container, terminate both instances, and delete the ECR repository, IAM roles and security groups
